newsitem.title: UK: PLO to pay family of 1985 ship hijacking victim.
newsitem.headline: PLO to pay family of 1985 ship hijacking victim.

text.p: The Palestine Liberation Organisation is to pay compensation to the family of American Leon Klinghoffer, shot dead during the hijacking of the Achille Lauro cruise ship in 1985, a lawyer for the PLO said on Tuesday.

Ramsay Clarke told the BBC World Service that lawyers for the Klinghoffer family had reached agreement with him on an out of court settlement of their civil suit against the PLO, weeks before it was due to go to court.
He declined to give details of the deal, but said: "It is full and final settlement that was amicably reached between the parties, and all are satisfied that it is fair and just."
Clarke said the agreement did not constitute an admission that the PLO was responsible for Klinghoffer's death.
Palestinian guerrillas seized the Italian cruise ship in 1985 and held the 400 people on board hostage.
They said they would blow up the 25,000-ton liner unless Israel agreed to release 50 Arab prisoners in its jails.
Klinghoffer, an elderly and crippled New York Jew, was the only person to die in the incident. He was shot while he sat in his wheelchair and his body was thrown into the sea.

After lengthy negotiations during which Egyptian leader Hosni Mubarak and PLO leader Yasser Arafat intervened, the hijackers left the ship on condition that they were flown to Tunis, where the PLO was based.

Clarke said of the legal settlement: "There is no admission whatsoever of responsibility or liability and the PLO maintains as it has throughout that it did everything that it could to prevent injury after it first learned of the seizure of the Achille Lauro."
He said compensation was offered because "reconciliation is desirable and the PLO recognises the pain and enduring sorrow of the Klinghoffer family, because it recognises the human tragedy involved."
He added: "It wants to live in peace with all people including the people who have been injured in these tragic years in the Middle East."
